title: AI-Augmented Research: Free to Write, Costly to Read
abstract: arXiv:2610.32355v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: We study a model in which artificial intelligence lowers the cost of writing faster than the cost of reading. Authors differ in reputation, and time-constrained readers, such as referees, choose between ignoring, verifying, and trusting papers. As writing costs fall, the band of verified papers shrinks: outsiders are no longer read, and established authors are no longer checked. In the ``costless writing limit,'' the share of verified papers vanishes, and a paper's impact depends on its author's reputation alone. Readers can escape the flood by asking AI to summarize the literature. These summaries aggregate papers reliably only if their errors are sufficiently independent. Once the share of papers written with the same AI exceeds a threshold, summaries inherit the AI's errors, and AI review filters out the original research that could correct them.

translated_title: AI增强的研究：写作无成本，阅读高代价
translated_abstract: 我们研究了一个模型，其中人工智能降低写作成本的速度快于降低阅读成本的速度。作者的声誉各不相同，而时间有限的读者（如审稿人）在忽略、验证和信任论文之间做出选择。随着写作成本的下降，被验证论文的范围缩小：无名作者的论文不再被阅读，知名作者的论文不再被核查。在“零成本写作极限”下，被验证论文的比例趋于消失，论文的影响力仅取决于其作者的声誉。读者可以通过让AI总结文献来逃离信息洪流。只有当这些总结中的错误足够相互独立时，它们才能可靠地聚合论文信息。一旦由同一AI撰写的论文比例超过某个阈值，这些总结就会继承该AI的错误，而AI评审会过滤掉本可以纠正这些错误的原创研究。
tldr: AI使写作成本骤降导致验证性阅读萎缩、论文影响力被作者声誉垄断；而当大量论文由同一AI生成时，AI文献总结会继承其系统性错误，并过滤掉本可纠错的原创研究。
en_tdlr: When AI makes writing nearly free, verification collapses and a paper's impact depends solely on its author's reputation; once too many papers are generated by the same AI, AI-produced summaries inherit its errors and filter out the original research that could correct them.
